title: The Film Without Spoken Words
fact_notes: 映画部の制作事例は架空。字幕・音声解説と芸術表現についての独自教材。

sentences.en: A high school film club decides to make a short movie that tells a story without using spoken dialogue.
sentences.ja: 高校の映画部は話し言葉の台詞を使わずに物語を伝える短編映画を制作することにします。

sentences.en: The students hope that viewers who speak different languages will be able to enjoy the same story.
sentences.ja: 生徒たちは異なる言語を話す観客が同じ物語を楽しめることを期待しています。

sentences.en: Their first scene shows a young musician searching for a lost instrument before an important performance.
sentences.ja: 最初の場面には大切な演奏の前に失くした楽器を探す若い音楽家が登場します。

sentences.en: However, when the club shows a rough version to classmates, some viewers cannot understand why the musician looks worried.
sentences.ja: しかし試作版を同級生に見せると、音楽家がなぜ不安そうなのか理解できない人もいます。

sentences.en: The students realize that removing words does not automatically make every part of a story easy to understand.
sentences.ja: 生徒たちは言葉を除けば物語のすべてが自動的にわかりやすくなるわけではないと気づきます。

sentences.en: They begin to investigate how images, movement, and sound communicate meaning even when characters say nothing.
sentences.ja: 登場人物が何も話さない場合でも画像、動き、音がどう意味を伝えるか調べ始めます。

sentences.en: The club first examines the position of people and objects inside each scene and the order in which events appear.
sentences.ja: 部はまず各場面内の人物と物の位置、出来事が現れる順番を調べます。

sentences.en: For example, showing an empty instrument case before the musician begins searching may explain the situation more clearly.
sentences.ja: 例えば音楽家が探し始める前に空の楽器ケースを見せると、状況がより明確になるかもしれません。

sentences.en: A close view of a worried face can suggest emotion, while a wider view can reveal important details in the surroundings.
sentences.ja: 心配そうな顔の近くからの映像は感情を示し、より広い映像は周囲の重要な細部を明らかにできます。

sentences.en: The students also notice that a scene's meaning may change when its order is altered.
sentences.ja: 生徒たちは場面の順序を変えると意味が変わる場合があることにも気づきます。

sentences.en: The film therefore becomes an experiment in selecting what an audience should notice at each moment.
sentences.ja: そのため映画は各瞬間に観客が何に注目すべきか選ぶ実験になります。

sentences.en: The club learns that visual storytelling requires careful choices rather than simply turning off the microphones.
sentences.ja: 映像で物語を伝えるにはマイクを切るだけでなく慎重な選択が必要だと学びます。

sentences.en: After improving the scenes, the students invite a different group of viewers to watch the movie and describe what they understood.
sentences.ja: 場面を改善した後、生徒たちは別の観客グループを招き、映画を見て理解したことを説明してもらいます。

sentences.en: Some viewers follow the story correctly, but others misunderstand the relationship between the musician and a person helping them.
sentences.ja: 物語を正しく追う人もいれば、音楽家と手伝う人の関係を誤解する人もいます。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, the club decides not to treat every difference in interpretation as evidence of failure.
sentences.ja: それでも部は解釈の違いをすべて失敗の証拠とみなさないことにします。

sentences.en: A story can reasonably invite several meanings, yet its central events should remain understandable to the intended audience.
sentences.ja: 物語は妥当な範囲で複数の意味を招き得ますが、中心となる出来事は対象の観客にわかるべきです。

sentences.en: The students revise a confusing scene while allowing viewers to form their own opinions about the characters' feelings.
sentences.ja: 生徒たちはわかりにくい場面を修正しつつ、登場人物の感情については観客自身が意見を持てるようにします。

sentences.en: This distinction helps them balance clarity with the creative freedom that gives art much of its value.
sentences.ja: この区別によって明確さと芸術の価値の多くを生む創造的自由を両立させやすくなります。

sentences.en: The club also discusses whether a film without dialogue is accessible to everyone or merely accessible in a different way.
sentences.ja: 部は台詞のない映画がすべての人に利用しやすいのか、それとも別の形で利用しやすいだけなのかも話し合います。

sentences.en: A viewer who cannot see the images clearly may need an audio description of important actions and visual details.
sentences.ja: 映像をはっきり見られない観客には重要な動作や視覚的細部の音声解説が必要かもしれません。

sentences.en: Another viewer may need clear written information about sounds that carry meaning, even when no one is speaking.
sentences.ja: 誰も話さなくても意味を持つ音について、明確な文字情報が必要な観客もいるかもしれません。

sentences.en: Instead of assuming that one design automatically serves every audience, the club considers different forms of support.
sentences.ja: 一つの設計ですべての観客に自動的に対応できると決めつけず、部は複数の支援方法を検討します。

sentences.en: They ask viewers with different needs to respond to possible additions before the film is released publicly.
sentences.ja: 映画を一般公開する前に、異なる必要のある観客に追加案への意見を求めます。

sentences.en: The experience shows that artistic choices and accessibility can be explored together rather than treated as unrelated concerns.
sentences.ja: この経験は芸術的な選択と利用しやすさを無関係の問題とせず一緒に検討できると示します。

sentences.en: At the final screening, the club presents the revised film along with optional explanations for viewers who want them.
sentences.ja: 最終上映で部は修正版の映画と、希望する観客向けの任意の解説を提供します。

sentences.en: The story still contains no spoken dialogue, but the students have become more careful about how its message may be received.
sentences.ja: 物語には今も話し言葉の台詞がありませんが、生徒たちはそのメッセージの受け取られ方により慎重になりました。

sentences.en: As a result, they no longer describe the absence of words as a guarantee of universal understanding.
sentences.ja: その結果、生徒たちは言葉がないことを普遍的な理解の保証とは説明しなくなります。

sentences.en: They explain that communication depends on the interaction between what creators express and what audiences can perceive.
sentences.ja: 伝達は作者が表現することと観客が知覚できることの相互作用に左右されると説明します。

sentences.en: The club is proud not because every viewer understands the film identically, but because more people can engage with its story.
sentences.ja: すべての観客が同じように理解するからではなく、より多くの人が物語に関われることを部は誇りに思います。

sentences.en: Their project suggests that creative freedom becomes richer when artists ask who might otherwise be left outside the experience.
sentences.ja: この活動は芸術家が誰が体験から取り残され得るかを問うと創造の自由がより豊かになると示唆します。

questions.prompt: What problem appears during the first screening?
options: Some viewers cannot understand the musician's worry.
All viewers already know the lost instrument's location.
Every student refuses to watch.
The film contains too much spoken dialogue.
questions.explanation_ja: 第1段落の「しかし試作版を同級生に見せると、音楽家がなぜ不安そうなのか理解できない人もいます。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: What does the club begin to investigate?
options: How to replace every camera with a microphone.
How to create longer spoken conversations.
How to write a school textbook.
How visual and sound choices communicate without dialogue.
questions.explanation_ja: 第1段落の「登場人物が何も話さない場合でも画像、動き、音がどう意味を伝えるか調べ始めます。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: How could the opening become clearer?
options: Remove every image of the instrument.
Place the ending before any introduction.
Show the empty instrument case before the search.
Show only the musician's shoes.
questions.explanation_ja: 第2段落の「例えば音楽家が探し始める前に空の楽器ケースを見せると、状況がより明確になるかもしれません。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: What does the author suggest about silent visual storytelling?
options: It is always understood identically by everyone.
It requires careful design rather than simply removing speech.
It cannot communicate any emotion.
It must contain a narrator.
questions.explanation_ja: 第2段落の「映像で物語を伝えるにはマイクを切るだけでなく慎重な選択が必要だと学びます。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: How does the club treat different interpretations?
options: Not all differences necessarily mean the film has failed.
Every different opinion is a mistake.
The viewers must agree on every emotion.
Only one classmate may interpret the film.
questions.explanation_ja: 第3段落の「それでも部は解釈の違いをすべて失敗の証拠とみなさないことにします。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: What balance does the club seek?
options: A completely fixed meaning for every detail.
No central events at all.
A ban on audience feedback.
Clear central events and room for creative interpretations.
questions.explanation_ja: 第3段落の「この区別によって明確さと芸術の価値の多くを生む創造的自由を両立させやすくなります。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: What may help viewers who cannot see details clearly?
options: Changing the school's timetable.
Showing fewer visual details without explanation.
Audio descriptions of relevant actions.
Removing all images and sound.
questions.explanation_ja: 第4段落の「映像をはっきり見られない観客には重要な動作や視覚的細部の音声解説が必要かもしれません。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: Why does the club consider different types of support?
options: Written information always replaces images perfectly.
One design does not guarantee accessibility for every viewer.
All audiences have identical needs.
Films without dialogue have no sounds.
questions.explanation_ja: 第4段落の「一つの設計ですべての観客に自動的に対応できると決めつけず、部は複数の支援方法を検討します。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: What does the club stop claiming about wordless films?
options: That lack of dialogue guarantees universal understanding.
That films can express emotions.
That a musician can be a character.
That viewers have different interpretations.
questions.explanation_ja: 第5段落の「伝達は作者が表現することと観客が知覚できることの相互作用に左右されると説明します。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: What is the passage's main idea?
options: A film must communicate one fixed interpretation.
Accessibility and artistry should never be considered together.
Removing spoken words always makes a film universally understandable.
Creative expression improves when artists consider how different audiences experience it.
questions.explanation_ja: 第5段落の「この活動は芸術家が誰が体験から取り残され得るかを問うと創造の自由がより豊かになると示唆します。」が根拠です。

grammar.focus: does not automatically make every part of a story easy to understand
grammar.explanation_ja: does not automaticallyは「自動的には〜ならない」という部分否定です。

grammar.focus: while a wider view can reveal important details
grammar.explanation_ja: whileは異なる映像の役割を対比します。

grammar.focus: while allowing viewers to form their own opinions
grammar.explanation_ja: while + 動名詞で同時に成り立つことを表します。

grammar.focus: not because every viewer understands the film identically, but because more people can engage
grammar.explanation_ja: not because A but because Bで理由を対比します。

discourse.role_ja: 言葉を除けば通じるという期待に対する困難です。
空のケースを先に見せる工夫の例です。
解釈の相違すべてが失敗ではないと示します。

paraphrases.source: The students realize that removing words does not automatically make every part of a story easy to understand.
paraphrases.rewrite: Removing dialogue does not ensure that a story is understood by everyone.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 台詞を消しても全員が理解する保証はありません。

paraphrases.source: The club learns that visual storytelling requires careful choices rather than simply turning off the microphones.
paraphrases.rewrite: Visual storytelling requires choices about what an audience notices.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 映像で伝えるには注意を向ける対象の設計が必要です。

paraphrases.source: The experience shows that artistic choices and accessibility can be explored together rather than treated as unrelated concerns.
paraphrases.rewrite: Artistic decisions and accessibility can be considered as connected issues.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 芸術と利用しやすさは同時に検討できます。

paraphrases.source: Their project suggests that creative freedom becomes richer when artists ask who might otherwise be left outside the experience.
paraphrases.rewrite: Creative work gains depth when artists consider people who may be excluded.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 取り残される人を考慮すると創造の幅が広がるという意味です。
